**RE: Member Appeal for Prior Authorization Denial**
*   **Member Name:** Taylor Kimura
*   **Member ID:** W381271109
*   **Plan:** Blue Shield of California (Commercial/ACA)
*   **Reference Number:** POC-972F74519C-71410
*   **Requested Service:** Total Knee Arthroplasty / Replacement (CPT 27447)
*   **Ordering Surgeon:** Okafor, MD
*   **Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-25

Dear Appeals Committee,

I am writing to formally appeal Blue Shield of California’s denial of the prior authorization request for a total knee replacement (CPT 27447), to be performed by Dr. Okafor. 

The denial letter dated August 25, 2026, states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." This determination was made under Blue Shield of California’s Medical Policy BSC7.10, "Knee Arthroplasty for Adults" (Effective Date: December 1, 2025). 

A review of my clinical history and my objective diagnostic imaging reveals that I completely satisfy all medical-necessity criteria outlined in Policy BSC7.10. Below, I map my medical records directly to your policy requirements to demonstrate why this denial should be reversed.

### 1. Correction of the Radiographic/Imaging Finding Denial
Policy BSC7.10 states that knee arthroplasty is medically necessary when:
> "F. The individual has one or more of the following conditions: 
> 1. Degenerative joint disease when all of the following conditions exist: ... 
> c. Radiographic evidence of severe osteoarthritis as evidenced by either of the following: 
> i. The presence of definite joint space narrowing with sclerosis and possible deformity of bone ends
> ii. The presence of large osteophytes, marked narrowing of joint space, severe sclerosis and definite deformity of the proximal tibia or distal femur"

**Clinical Evidence:** 
My weight-bearing knee radiographs dated 2026-06-25 demonstrate:
*   **Bone-on-bone apposition** in both the medial and patellofemoral compartments. Bone-on-bone contact represents the most severe form of "definite joint space narrowing" possible.
*   **Lateral joint-space narrowing**.
*   **Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4 osteoarthritis**, which is the highest possible grade on this clinical scale, representing severe osteophyte formation, severe joint space narrowing, and deformity of the bone ends.

These imaging findings clearly exceed the policy threshold of "definite joint space narrowing" and "marked narrowing of joint space" required under Section I.F.1.c. 

### 2. Clinical Indications and Physical Examination Criteria
Policy BSC7.10 requires:
> "A. The reason for the arthroplasty is osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis, osteonecrosis, or post-traumatic arthritis of the knee joint"
And:
> "b. Documentation of limited range of motion, antalgic gait, and pain in knee joint with passive range of motion on physical examination"

**Clinical Evidence:**
*   **Diagnosis:** Severe osteoarthritis of the knee joint (satisfying Section I.A).
*   **Symptom Duration & Severity:** I have suffered from 14 months of progressive pain in my knee, which is unrelieved by rest. My pain is so severe that it wakes me 3 to 4 times nightly, and I cannot climb stairs without assistance.
*   **Physical Examination Findings:** Dr. Okafor’s physical examination notes show varus alignment, crepitus, and effusion of the knee joint. My passive range of motion is severely restricted, measuring only 5 to 100 degrees (satisfying the requirement for "limited range of motion" and "pain in knee joint with passive range of motion" under Section I.F.1.b).

### 3. Exhaustion of Conservative Therapy
Policy BSC7.10 requires:
> "a. Documentation of unsuccessful conservative therapy (non-surgical medical management), or documentation of rationale if conservative therapy is considered inappropriate"
The "Policy Guidelines" section further details that non-surgical treatment should include anti-inflammatory medications, physical therapy, and therapeutic injections, as appropriate.

**Clinical Evidence:**
I have fully exhausted all conservative treatment options without obtaining adequate relief:
*   **Supervised Physical Therapy:** I participated in a supervised physical therapy program focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion for 14 weeks (from 2026-04-28 to 2026-08-04), completing 18 visits. This is fully documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
*   **Medication:** I used oral NSAIDs for 4 months, which provided completely inadequate relief.
*   **Therapeutic Injection:** On 2026-06-04, I received a corticosteroid injection in my knee, which only provided a brief 3 weeks of partial relief.

### 4. Exclusion of Contraindications
My medical records confirm that I have no active infections, no untreated substance use disorders, and I am a non-smoker. Furthermore, my BMI is 29, meaning I do not meet the "morbid obesity (BMI greater than 40)" relative contraindication outlined in the Policy Guidelines.

### Conclusion
The clinical and radiographic data submitted clearly show that I have severe, bone-on-bone (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade 4) osteoarthritis of the knee joint that has failed to respond to extensive conservative therapy (including 18 physical therapy sessions, oral NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection). My daily functioning and sleep are severely impaired. 

All criteria under Blue Shield of California Medical Policy BSC7.10 have been met. I respectfully request that you reverse this denial and approve the prior authorization for my total knee replacement (CPT 27447) so that I may proceed with surgery under the care of Dr. Okafor.

Please find attached my weight-bearing knee radiograph report (2026-06-25), my physical therapy discharge summary, and Dr. Okafor's clinical exam notes.

Thank you for your timely reconsideration of this matter.

Sincerely,

Taylor Kimura
